name: Arecibo Observatory
description: Home of a 305-metre spherical reflector dish built in a natural sinkhole; the dish collapsed on 1 December 2020 and will not be rebuilt. The site is still an operating observatory with a 12-metre radio telescope for VLBI, a LIDAR facility and a visitor center.
highlights: In 1964, soon after it opened, it showed that Mercury turns once every 59 days, not 88 as had been thought.
In 1974 Russell Hulse and Joseph Taylor found the first binary pulsar there, work later recognised with the Nobel Prize in Physics.
Aleksander Wolszczan discovered the pulsar PSR B1257+12 there and later found planets orbiting it, among the first known beyond the Solar System.
film: Arecibo appears in Contact (1997), the film of Carl Sagan's novel about a radio signal from another star.
